findings.message: Instance fix. The WeakSet stops hand-built literals, but the factory that mints trust is still public. `contextFor` is exported from `@amax/core/server`, and every module, chat intent and MCP tool may import that package; `modules/hr/server/jobs.ts` already calls `contextFor.job` from module code. Any caller can therefore run `contextFor.job(anyTenantId, "anything")` and get a context that `isSystemContext` accepts. That context reads unmasked salary, EPF and bank data through getEmployment and passes inScope and applyStatusDates. The audit row records a job name the caller made up. The issued object is also not frozen. Only `actor.kind` is checked again, so `ctx.actor.id`, `tenantId` and `onBehalfOf` can be changed after issue and the context still passes. Fix: only the job runner (runDueJobs or the workflow engine) should be able to mint system contexts, through an unexported capability or a factory that is not on the module import surface. The runner then hands the context to the job handler. Freeze the issued context and its actor. Add a test showing that module-level code can't get an accepted system context.
findings.scenario: An MCP tool handler in any module calls `getEmployment(tx, personId, contextFor.job(tenantId, "payroll.sync"))` → it gets the unmasked base_salary, epf_number and bank_account for any entity, and the audit says job:payroll.sync.

findings.message: This round didn't touch the earlier carry-forward finding. Later periods are still compared with the value in force at `effectiveOn` instead of with the period just before each one. A planned return to the old value is therefore overwritten. Fix: walk the later periods in starts_on order and stop carrying a column at the first period whose value differs from its predecessor. Add a table test with a step down and then a step back up.
findings.scenario: FTE 1.0 from Jan, 0.6 from Mar, 1.0 from Jun. Then changePerson sets fte 0.8 from Feb → the June period is rewritten to 0.8 and the planned return to full time is lost.

findings.message: This round didn't touch the earlier leaver-audit finding, and the README in this diff still says later periods 'are removed … (pay values left out)'. recordLeaver still hard-deletes later periods. Its audit leaves out base_salary, currency, epf_number, bank_name, bank_account and the row ids, and it doesn't record the old `ends_on` of the period in force. A mistaken leaver can't be undone. Fix: end and void the later periods instead of deleting them, or keep the full rows somewhere they can be restored from. Record the before-value of `ends_on` for every period the update changes.
findings.scenario: A person has a planned raise from 2027-01-01. HR records them as leaving on 2026-11-30 by mistake → the raise row is deleted, and neither the table nor the audit keeps its salary or the old end date of the current period.

findings.message: The department-scope finding is still open, and the class includes a second copy. inScope (the write path) still calls `assertCan(v, action, { legalEntityId })` without the row's department. The README in this diff claims viewers are limited to 'the legal entities and departments their hr:read reaches', but this diff doesn't change `sees` in contracts.ts either. Fix: build one scope subject (legalEntityId, department and any other scope dimension) shared by `sees`, masking and inScope. Add department-scoped cases to both the read and the write scoping tests.
findings.scenario: An HR assignment scoped to entity LK, departments ['Engineering'], calls changePerson on an LK Finance employee → it isn't refused, because the department is never passed to assertCan.
